name: Armodafinil
summary: The R-form of modafinil: a prescription wakefulness drug for sleep disorders, used off-label for focus with little direct evidence in healthy people.
what_it_is: Armodafinil, sold as Nuvigil, is a prescription drug that promotes wakefulness. Modafinil is a 50-50 mix of two mirror-image forms of the same molecule; armodafinil is one of them, the R-form. It is approved for adults with excessive sleepiness from obstructive sleep apnea, narcolepsy or shift work disorder, and it is a Schedule IV controlled substance.

evidence.why: It is approved for sleepiness from three sleep disorders; for focus in rested healthy people, the evidence comes from studies of modafinil, which found only small effects on a few kinds of thinking tests.

status_us.label: FDA-approved for sleep disorders; Schedule IV
status_us.note: Nuvigil is approved to improve wakefulness in adults with excessive sleepiness from obstructive sleep apnea (it treats the sleepiness, not the airway obstruction), narcolepsy or shift work disorder. It is a Schedule IV controlled substance, it is not approved for children, and use for focus is off-label.

benefits.claim: Improves wakefulness in adults with excessive sleepiness from obstructive sleep apnea, narcolepsy or shift work disorder (approved use)

Evidence for focus in rested people comes from modafinil, its parent mixture: across 19 placebo-controlled trials the overall effect on thinking tests was small, and another set of meta-analyses found a clear gain only in memory updating

risks.risk: Headache (17% versus 9% on placebo), nausea (7% versus 3%), dizziness (5% versus 2%) and insomnia (5% versus 1%) in trials
Serious rash, including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, has required hospital care; in children given modafinil, rash led to stopping in about 8 in 1,000; any new rash needs prompt medical review
Allergic and multi-organ reactions, including angioedema, anaphylaxis and DRESS (a drug reaction with rash, fever and organ involvement)
Psychiatric effects: anxiety, agitation and irritability led some trial patients to stop, and mania, delusions, hallucinations, suicidal thoughts and aggression have been reported
Small rises in blood pressure and pulse; the label advises against use with a history of left ventricular hypertrophy, or with mitral valve prolapse that caused symptoms on stimulants before
Misuse, physical dependence and tolerance have been reported

avoid_if: Pregnant or planning pregnancy (animal data suggest harm, and fetal growth restriction and miscarriage have been reported)
Heart disease, left ventricular hypertrophy, or mitral valve prolapse that caused symptoms on stimulants (needs a clinician first)
History of psychosis, depression or mania (needs a clinician first)
Athletes in tested sports: WADA bans modafinil in competition and covers all optical isomers of stimulants, and armodafinil is one of the two mirror-image forms of modafinil
interactions: Hormonal birth control: may be less effective during use and for one month after stopping
Drugs cleared by the liver enzyme CYP2C19: they may stay in the body longer
Drugs cleared by the liver enzymes CYP3A4/5: they may be cleared faster and work less well
Warfarin: more frequent INR checks may be needed; MAO inhibitors: use with caution

labs.why: The sources reviewed set no routine blood tests; the label says closer monitoring of heart rate and blood pressure may be appropriate.

studies.title: NUVIGIL (armodafinil) tablets: prescribing information
studies.people: Adults with obstructive sleep apnea, narcolepsy or shift work disorder (645 on armodafinil in pooled placebo-controlled trials)
studies.finding: Approved to improve wakefulness; headache was the most common side effect (17% versus 9%), and the label warns about serious rash, psychiatric symptoms and reduced birth-control effectiveness.

studies.title: The Efficacy of Modafinil as a Cognitive Enhancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
studies.people: 19 placebo-controlled trials, 767 adults who were not sleep-deprived (modafinil, not armodafinil)
studies.finding: Modafinil had a small overall effect on cognition (g = 0.10), mainly on executive function and processing speed; the authors saw only limited potential as a cognitive enhancer in rested people.

ask_your_clinician: Is my sleepiness from a sleep disorder that needs diagnosis and treatment first?
Will armodafinil weaken my birth control or change the levels of my other medicines?
Do my heart or mental-health history make it unsafe for me?

sources.title: The Efficacy of Modafinil as a Cognitive Enhancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sources.publisher: Journal of Clinical Psychopharmacology (copy hosted at gwern.net)

sources.title: How effective are pharmaceuticals for cognitive enhancement in healthy adults? A series of meta-analyses of cognitive performance during acute administration of modafinil, methylphenidate and D-amphetamine

notes_for_editor: No study of armodafinil for focus in rested healthy people was found within the search budget; the focus evidence is borrowed from modafinil meta-analyses and graded 'limited' for that reason. The label was read from the Drugs.com copy (revised February 2025); the last ~7% of the page was not read. 'Fetal harm based on animal data' appears in the label Highlights; section 8.1 reports growth restriction and miscarriage. WADA's 2026 list names modafinil (S6.A, in competition) and the related fladrafinil and flmodafinil but not armodafinil; whether armodafinil falls under the 'similar' wording of S6 was not checked.
